narrative:
## 2026 — the year the vault learned to rewrite itself

This was the year the question changed. It started as *how do I take better notes* and became *what would a knowledge base do if it could think alongside me*.

Three threads ran through everything. The first was **legibility** — the recurring insistence that a system you can't see into is a system you can't trust, which showed up in the agent-confidence work as much as in the writing about institutions. The second was **the cost of attention**: the year's most-edited notes all circle the same anxiety, that the scarce resource was never information but the bandwidth to review it. The third was the one that surprised me — **tools that rewrite themselves**, the slow realization that the interesting move wasn't automating capture but automating curation.

What crystallized: engram itself, shipped in the autumn after a spring of design docs. What was abandoned: the chat UI, quietly, once it became clear that a conversational front-end was the wrong shape for a thinking tool. What shifted: the whole posture moved from theory to practice — the notes from January argue about epistemics; the notes from November are commit messages.

The through-line, if there is one, is that the year was spent building the thing that would make next year's reflection easier to write.
